Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary and for the questionnaire. Quick answers and context from our side:

- Backup retention: We typically ask for a max retention cap of 90 days for snapshots/backups, and a guarantee that customer-initiated deletions are removed from active storage within 30 days. We understand deleted items may remain in immutable backups for a bounded window; please specify that window.
- Primary data deletion SLA: we need confirmation that when a record is deleted via API or account deletion, it is removed from active storage within 30 days and subsequently from backups within a hard cap (ideally 90 days).
- Logs: our audit policy requires searchable log retention for 12 months, with the ability to export relevant logs for e-discovery within 7 business days.
- HIPAA / BAA: as a healthcare customer we will require a BAA; please confirm Redwood’s stance and whether BAAs are available for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private deployments.
- SOC 2: please share whatever report you can via a secure link/portal — procurement will review the Type II controls covering encryption, key management, and change control.

Thanks — jumping in with the technical clarifications so procurement has concrete answers to reference. High-level summary (happy to cover specifics on the call):

- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering the inference platform control environment. We provide a secure, time-limited link for the report and can redline an NDA if needed before full access. I’ll share the link through our secure portal after this thread.

- HIPAA / BAA: We support HIPAA-compliant deployments. BAAs are available for Dedicated and Private deployments by default; for Hosted we can execute a BAA where the deployment and contractual terms meet our compliance requirements — we’ll provide the BAA template for your legal team to review.

- Primary data deletion SLA: Our standard commitment is that customer-visible data is removed from active storage within 30 days of a deletion request. For immutable backups, we maintain a retention lifecycle — default snapshot retention is 90 days. We can configure shorter retention windows for Dedicated/Private customers as part of the onboarding contract.

- Backup propagation & deletion caveat: snapshots are immutable for the snapshot period to preserve recoverability. That means deleted objects could appear in a snapshot until that snapshot expires. We can implement accelerated snapshot truncation as a supported option for Dedicated/Private customers with contractual SLAs; for Hosted customers we can offer a best-effort accelerated purge and provide timelines in scope of the contract.

- Log retention: default searchable logs are retained 90 days in the console; for customers requiring 12-month retention we offer an extended logs tier (retention up to 13 months) as an add-on with export APIs for e-discovery. We can commit to producing exports for requested time windows within 7 business days (subject to add-on terms and the volume of data).

- Encryption / KMS: Data at rest is encrypted; customers can use Redwood-managed keys or bring-your-own-keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private deployments. Key rotation and destruction policies are documented in the SOC2 materials.

Next steps I’ll take today:
1) Share SOC2 portal link (time-limited) and BAA template via our secure portal.
2) Review the procurement form and call out any questions/necessary redlines.

If you want specific wording for contract language around backup retention windows and a hard deletion SLA for backups, flag that and we’ll draft proposed contract clauses for procurement.

— Markus
